newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's president wants to be top Latin crooner.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's president wants to be top Latin crooner.

text.p: President Abdala Bucaram, who released his debut CD this week, said he wants to outsell top Mexican romantic crooner Luis Miguel.

"I know that in this production you aren't going to find a great singer like Luis Miguel but I hope to sell as much as he does," Ecuador's president said, as quoted by daily Hoy on Friday. He added that he put heart into his rock 'n' roll.

Bucaram described how he used to seduce women by playing tapes of the Uruguayan group Los Iracundos, who are now his backing band. "When I was a young man and wanted to conquer a woman, I put on a Los Iracundos cassette and they surrendered. That's how I made my wife fall in love with me," he explained.

Bucaram launched his first CD, "A Madman in Love," featuring his original songs, at a concert in the port city of Guayaquil on Wednesday. He belted out the tunes wearing a black shirt and flanked by young female back-up singers in tight-fitting midriff outfits.
The president said he sold 12,000 CDs at the concert and the disc is on its way going golden. He said he has another 13 songs in reserve that werec not included in his 18-track CD.

The CD cover features the Ecuadorean flag and Bucaram wearing his presidential sash. Proceeds are going to charity, but his foray into the world of pop has attracted criticism from some Ecuadorans, who argue that he should spend more time on his country's rampant poverty.

Rock 'n' roll featured heavily in Bucaram's election campaign, which culminated in his July victory on a populist ticket. The president, who first presented two songs from his CD at a beauty contest a few weeks ago, said that from now on he will sing only for "very noble" causes.
